annotations.text:
ONE JOB PER FRAME

Read left to right: connect to a site, see what it offers, jump if you already know where you are going, fill the form, watch it run, read what came back — or what went wrong — then what you have done, and under that, what actually crossed the wire.

Compose (4), Running (5), Result (6) and Failed (7) are the same geometry. The tool name never moves. The form does not sit above the result; it becomes it, then becomes the failure. That is why no single frame is crowded even as the feature count goes up.

THE BAR IS THE ROUTER

SURVEY · COMPOSE · RECORD sit top-left on every screen, the current one lit. Any place is one click from any screen, and you can always tell where you are. COMPOSE is dimmed until a tool is picked, which is honest rather than disabled-looking.

This replaced WEBMCP in the bar — the OS titlebar already says that (main.rs:1232), so the row was carrying a word the window repeats. Navigation cost nothing.

Record's two altitudes are a visible RUNS / EVERYTHING toggle now, not the hidden ⌥ hint I had before. Same mistake as ⌘K-only discovery: a keystroke nobody can see is not a route.

WHY NOT A SIDEBAR

Of the nine frames, only three are places. Running, Result and Failed are Compose's own lifecycle — you never navigate to an outcome. Summon is an overlay. Connect is Survey with no page. Log is Record at another altitude.

Three destinations do not earn a permanent rail, and a rail would reintroduce exactly the disease diagnosed in V1: window permanently spent on a decision already made.

⌘K alone was not enough either — that is the recall-versus-recognition trap. The bar gives recognition for the three places; ⌘K gives speed for the hundreds of tools behind them.

VERIFICATION

Every capability read out of main.rs and commands.rs, plus everything the approved plan adds, mapped to the frame that draws it. Navigation is now its own group at the top.

The rule at the bottom is the one I broke twice: I listed things as covered on the strength of hints I had never drawn — protocol detail, schema expansion, nested fields. All three are real frames now.

Four items stay in accent. They are open decisions, not omissions.

LIGHT — FIVE TOKENS MOVE, NOTHING ELSE

Same frame, same geometry, same rhythm as Compose. Only paper, ink, mute, hair and accent change, which is the whole argument for putting them behind a Theme value instead of the consts they are today.

Roles invert, hues do not: warm off-white ground, warm near-black ink. The accent is the one value that could not simply flip — #C45C3A on light paper measures 3.6:1, under AA. Darkened to #A8452A for 5.0:1. Error text must never be the least readable thing on screen.

Reached from ⌘K, not from a switch parked in a corner. It is a preference, not a place.
